summary: Prevents anonymous signup from probing or refreshing a browser session while preserving login restoration and protected-route session recovery.
userImpact: Anonymous signup no longer emits expected unauthorized session requests or related browser-console noise.
Login pages still restore valid cookie sessions, and protected application routes continue to refresh expired access before redirecting to login.
security: Public authentication routing uses one shared exact-path policy for session bootstrap and unauthorized-response handling so newly supported public paths cannot silently drift between those controls.
Only root signup and established invitation enrollment suppress the initial session probe; login remains session-aware and protected routes retain fail-closed validation, refresh, and redirection.
documentation: The generated technical release notes describe the public authentication session-bootstrap correction and protected-route compatibility.
rollback: Redeploy the previous frontend image or frontend host package; no API, configuration, or database rollback is required.
validation: Focused frontend tests cover root signup, established invitation enrollment, session-aware login and recovery pages, protected-route session validation, expired-session refresh, and exact path-boundary matching.
Browser coverage verifies that anonymous signup renders without authentication or refresh probes and that a valid cookie session on login is restored and redirected without browser diagnostics.
